subject: can a radio button setting be changed progromatically

messages.author: 566ab60ba4d979e5
messages.subject: can a radio button setting be changed progromatically
parts:
I am programming a shiny app which allow the user to choose train and test data as well as other settings, In return, the user gets optimal prediction model.
One of the radio buttons in the app is "allow computing" button which if pressed will make the code in my server work for finding the optimal model.
My wish is to set back this button to " no " after the model is shown and keep the output without the need to wait for user intervention.
can i do that?

messages.author: 4317e7b9c140bf2d
messages.subject: Re: can a radio button setting be changed progromatically
parts:
Basel - there are two ways to do this. The simple one, which is the one you're probably looking for, is the Shiny function updateRadioButtons().

Alternatively, you can re-render the output the radio button is in. Assuming the initial value of the radio button is hard-coded and not a variable, that will also restore the buttons to their initial value. To force a re-render of the output, it needs to include something "reactive." Change that and the output will be re-rendered. The reactive value doesn't have to actually appear in the output, something like this will work:

output$xxx <- renderUI([
    x <- rv$render_xxx         # you don't have to actually use "x" for anything
   taglist(
      # what you want to render goes here
   )
})
